description.narrative: Insatsen avser humanitärt stöd genom World Food Program (WFP) för perioden 2019-2021. WFP har varit en regelbunden partner för genomförandet av Sidas humanitära insatser senast genom ett flerårigt avtal för perioden 2015-2017, samt ett avtal för 2018. Det föreslås nu att återigen ingå ett treårigt avtal för att öka förutsägbarhet och flexibilitet i samarbetet. Av 2019 års stöd från Sida, totalt 151 MSEK, avses 96 MSEK att användas för WFP:s huvudverksamhet varav 90 MSEK till akuta matsäkerhetsinsatser och 6 MSEK till kapacitetsstöd. Resterande 55 MSEK avses användas till finansiering av United Nations Humanitarian Air Services (UNHAS) för att förbättra tillträde till människor i behov av humanitär hjälp.

This contribution entails humanitarian support through the World Food Program (WFP) for the period 2019-2021. WFP has been a regular partner for the implementation of Sida's humanitarian assistance through a multi-year agreement for the period 2015-2017, and an agreement for 2018. It is hereby proposed to enter into a new three-year agreement to increase predictability and flexibility of the cooperation. Of 2019 years' support from Sida, amounting to a total of 151 million SEK, 96 million SEK will be distributed for WFP's core activities, including 90 MSEK for emergency food security interventions and 6 MSEK for capacity strengthening, while the remaining SEK 55 million will be used to finance the United Nations Humanitarian Air Services (UNHAS) to improve access to people in need of humanitarian aid.

The objective of this contribution is to provide life-saving assistance to people affected by food insecurity and malnutrition through support to WFP's humanitarian operations in a number of countries, annually identified by Sida's humanitarian Unit during the course of the allocation process or as a response to sudden changes in the humanitarian situation in-country. The contribution from Sida will mainly be used for (i) food assistance, (ii) targeted nutrition interventions and (iii) transport and logistics on behalf of the whole humanitarian community.

Sida's support to WFP within this agreement is for humanitarian assistance, meaning there are no overall results for the period, but output results and achievements on an annual basis. A few examples from each annual report are summarised below, for additional information please see statements on reports from each respective year.
2019 In Yemen WFP managed to reach 12 million people with food assistance during active conflict in a challenging environment. In Sudan despite diminishing funding levels WFP managed to contribute to lower the levels of Moderate Acute Malnutrition from 89,6% to 93,3%.
2020 WFP continuously supported South Sudanese refugees throughout the region. In Kenya for example, WFP managed to reach 425 000 refugees with food assistance through cash assistance, vouchers and in-kind food assistance. A positive note is that that gender and protection analysis informed programme cycle on activities tailored to the needs, capacities and priorities of the affected population.
2021 In 2021 WFP introduced cash assistance in Central African Republic with positive feedback from communities. 92% of beneficiaries stated that the preferred modality is cash in envelope. In DRC WFP supported partners rehabilitation of roads and other physical infrastructure in order to restore access to previously hard-to-reach places.
UNHAS Sida has through the agreement with WFP allocated more than 200 MSEK to UNHAS activities in multiple crises. UNHAS supports the humanitarian community to access people in need in hard to reach locations, both through transport of personnel and cargo. In many crises humanitarian assistance would not be possible without the functioning of UNHAS. During the Covid-19 pandemic UNHAS in many situations was the only operating air transport to make sure assistance could reach people in need.
Protection strategy Additionally Sida has supported WFP for its work on enhancing protection policy and mainstreaming within the whole organisation over the course of the agreement period. WFP has decided upon its first ever protection mainstreaming strategy as part of this work and will during the course of the next agreement continue roll-out and capacity strengthening at country offices. Throughout this agreement period Sida has identified weak to non-existent reporting on protection issues in the annual country reports meaning that an increased focus on protection mainstreaming through the implementation of this plan at country level should be a priority for WFP. This is something Sida will continue follow in order to make sure WFP stays true to its commitment to incorporate protection within all its work.
WFP was named the Nobel Peace Prize Laureate in 2020, with the motivation: "for its efforts to combat hunger, for its contribution to bettering conditions for peace in conflict-affected areas and for acting as a driving force in efforts to prevent the use of hunger as a weapon of war and conflict." The Prize gave due recognition of the inexorable link between peace and food security, and provided an energizing boost to WFP's employees as they stayed and delivered in frequently shifting field of operations affected by COVID-19, conflict and climate change. The naming of WFP as Nobel Peace Prize Laureate has led to a redoubling of its efforts to continue providing principled and high-quality assistance to affected communities and their governments. It is however too early to say whether WFP's fund-raising has benefited from the Prize.
